name: terminal-ui
title: Terminal UI
description: A scripted CLI onboarding inside a fake terminal window. Shimmering purple bars spell out scanning and profiling steps with percentages, then status lines type themselves out and further bars and rules follow.
use: A developer onboarding or wait screen wants a terminal aesthetic while the product pretends to get ready.
avoid: Every label, line and timing is hardcoded, and the bar enforces a 520px minimum width that overflows narrow columns.
a11y: The scripted text has no live region or role, so screen readers never hear progress or the messages. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark violet terminal inside window chrome with three traffic-light dots and a zsh path label. Rows of monospace characters glow purple as filled progress bars, each with a small star icon and token count, and dashed rules divide sections.
behaves: A bar crawls to full while its label and percentage change and a highlight sweeps across the letters, the icon pulsing in step. Status lines then type out character by character behind a blinking caret, and the next divider and bar begin before the sequence stops.
customise: Only a completion callback, a class name and inline styles are exposed; the phases, labels, icons and timings all live in a hardcoded sequence array.
weight: moderate: A forty-frame-per-second loop repaints every character cell of each bar while typing timers run.
